The SKY Accumulation Percentage escapes the SBE-BEAM's bound

title: The SP-BEAM bounds delegated rate changes on four axes at once, giving a whitelisted operator a rate of change rather than a free hand
content:
A.3.7.1.3 lets Governance-whitelisted operators adjust vault Stability Fees, the Dai Savings Rate and the Sky Savings Rate directly, constrained by four per-rate parameters: `min`, `max`, `step`, and `tau`.

The four do different work. `min` and `max` (A.3.7.1.3.1.1, A.3.7.1.3.1.2) bound the *level* in both directions. `step` (A.3.7.1.3.1.3) "limits how much the rates can be increased or decreased in a single transaction in basis points, bound by the `tau` parameter," and `tau` (A.3.7.1.3.1.4) sets the minimum interval between operations — currently 57,600 seconds, or 16 hours. Together the last two express a maximum *speed*: at most `step` basis points per `tau`, in either direction.

That combination is what makes delegation tolerable. A level bound alone would let an operator jump a rate from `min` to `max` in one transaction; a speed bound alone would let it drift arbitrarily far given time. Bounding both means any move large enough to matter takes long enough for governance to observe and intervene.

Note the contrast with the Smart Burn Engine's SBE-BEAM (A.3.5.2.4), whose value bounds are deliberately one-sided. Here the bounds are symmetric, because for interest rates both directions carry risk: too high strangles borrowing demand, too low forfeits revenue and weakens the peg. There is no safe direction to leave unbounded.

A.3.7.1.3.1.2.1 adds a fail-closed backstop beneath the configuration: regardless of `max`, the module cannot set a rate above 50% (5,000 basis points) and such attempts revert — with the advice that `max` "should not be set to a value higher than 50%... to avoid confusion," conceding that governance config and technical reality can otherwise disagree.
description: Each rate has its own min, max and per-transaction step in basis points, and tau (currently 16 hours) gates consecutive operations, so step over tau fixes a maximum drift speed.
